reasoning.Student B:

However, most applicants prefer y > x > w > z. This means z will be very competitive, and my low priority at w makes it unlikely I'll get in there unless it's a last resort.

Since my priority is 1 at both x and z, and most applicants prefer y and x, I believe my best strategy is to rank x as my first choice. Ranking z first might lead to me missing out on x entirely if many others also rank z highly and I don't get matched.

After x, I'll rank z as my second choice, as it's still my most preferred school if I can get it. Then y, and finally w. This strategy balances my personal preferences with the likely competitive landscape. I am prioritizing getting *a* good school over holding out for my absolute top choice that may be unattainable.
